gates.rule: Every retained rating must map to exactly one planned item, rater, monitoring class, and domain; duplicate rating identities are forbidden.

gates.construct: minimum independent replication per rated object
gates.rule: Every analyzed item must retain at least four distinct rater ratings, and at least 95% of items must retain five or more ratings.
gates.rationale: The design plans six ratings per item. Four is a fail-closed floor chosen to survive two-rater loss by construction; it is not a validated reliability threshold.

gates.construct: coverage of the rater facet used by the bootstrap data-generating process
gates.rule: At least ten of twelve raters must remain active overall; every monitoring class and every confirmatory domain must include at least eight active raters.
gates.rationale: The gate permits at most two complete rater losses overall while preventing a class or domain from being supported by a narrow rater subset. These values are provisional simulation thresholds.

gates.construct: comparability of monitoring-class exposure after missingness
gates.rule: Each class must retain at least 80% of its planned assignments, and the largest minus smallest class retention fraction must not exceed 0.10.

gates.construct: comparability and support across confirmatory content domains
gates.rule: Each confirmatory domain must retain at least 75% of planned assignments; within every class, the largest minus smallest domain retention fraction must not exceed 0.15.
gates.rationale: This gate is designed to detect domain-selective attrition before a pooled effect is reported. Thresholds require prospective calibration and are not claims of psychometric sufficiency.

gates.construct: linkage of item and rater facets
gates.rule: The retained item-rater bipartite graph, overall rater co-rating graph, and every class-specific rater co-rating graph must be connected. No connected component may be silently dropped.
gates.rationale: Connectivity is necessary for linkage but does not establish adequate precision, reliability, or absence of selection bias.

gates.construct: defined restricted-wild test under the retained structure
gates.rule: The observed two-way variance must be positive and no more than 10% of exact Rademacher patterns may have nonpositive bootstrap variance.
gates.rationale: This preserves the current provisional inferential fail-closed rule. The 10% threshold remains unvalidated and must be sensitivity-tested.

prohibited_interpretations: Passing these gates validates the semantic-fidelity construct.
Graph connectivity proves unbiasedness or adequate reliability.
A defined p-value makes informative dropout ignorable.
A failed gate permits deletion of affected items, raters, or domains followed by an unqualified confirmatory analysis.
These thresholds are empirically validated operating standards.
